clue.text: Hard on horse being transported to get into a small space

indicators.note: things transported are carried off and moved about, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A horse is being loaded into a cramped horsebox, and it is hard going.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoehorn something is to squeeze it, with effort, into a space barely big enough for it.

clue.text: Half the people are not quite generally known

parts.note: semi is the prefix for half
the public is the people at large

explanation.surface: Half the population is only partly aware of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Something semipublic is partly open, so its information is shared with some people but not everyone.

clue.text: Having a task to fulfil, André ran on out

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so the letters are put in a fresh order

parts.note: the letters of all three words, accent dropped

explanation.surface: André dashes off because he has a job to do.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on an errand is to be sent out on a short trip to perform a particular task.

clue.text: I hit a storm in the Caribbean

definitions.note: the answer is a country; the definition names where it lies

indicators.note: a storm throws everything into turmoil, so the letters are tossed about

parts.note: the letters of all three words

explanation.surface: A sailor runs into a hurricane while in the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: Haiti is a country on the island of Hispaniola, in the Caribbean Sea.

clue.text: With this there's no doorstop!

parts.note: surface reading: a wedge that holds a door open
setter's reading: someone holding this permission cannot be stopped at the door

explanation.walkthrough: 'doorstop' is split in sense into 'stop at the door'; a legal entitlement to go in means nobody may halt you there.
explanation.definitionFit: A right of entry is a legal entitlement to enter premises, so the holder cannot be barred.

clue.text: Has skill to develop road at city centre

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective, 'having skill'; the clue's verb form is loose

indicators.note: to develop something is to change its form, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, so only its middle letters are kept

parts.note: the two middle letters of city

explanation.surface: A planner shows expertise by building a road into the middle of a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means clever or skilful, especially with the hands; the clue loosely phrases that as a verb.

clue.text: A literary protector cuts out in a Cinque Port

indicators.note: in places one set of letters inside the other

parts.note: Dover is one of the Cinque Ports, a historic group of English Channel harbour towns

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so the letters are put in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A book protector is being trimmed in a south coast port.
explanation.definitionFit: A dust cover, or dust jacket, is the removable paper wrapper that protects a book.

clue.text: Work with a number in a shop, usefully

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of shop and the start of usefully

explanation.surface: Someone does a job alongside a colleague in a shop, to good effect.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical work, and composers' works are catalogued by opus number.

clue.text: The millions, but not including us!

definitions.note: those people, the others besides us

parts.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for million; that the letters then also run straight across the clue's opening is a coincidence of this charade, not a hidden word

explanation.surface: The masses, set apart from our own group.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the phrase 'us and them', the masses versus ourselves.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun refers to other people, a group that excludes the speaker and listeners.

clue.text: Translations of gin names

parts.note: the letters of both words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is translating the brand names of gins into another language.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no separate anagram signal: 'Translations' does double duty, as the definition and as the hint that the letters of gin names are turned into something else.
explanation.definitionFit: A translation renders what words signify, so translations are senses or interpretations of a text.

clue.text: A university test turns out to be cunning

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something that turns out is twisted into a different shape, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: U is the standard abbreviation for university
taken as written

explanation.surface: A university exam proves to be a crafty one.
explanation.definitionFit: Astute and cunning are synonyms for shrewd, sharp-witted and quick to see an advantage.

clue.text: In which there are two sides: on and off

definitions.text: In which there are two sides: on and off

parts.note: surface reading: something switched on and off, like a light

parts.words: In which there are two sides
parts.note: setter's reading: a game between two teams, whose field divides into the on side and off side

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the on side (or leg side) and the off side, relative to the batsman's stance.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket game is played between two teams, and its field has an on side and an off side.

clue.text: Relating to time before CDs? No, in fact before there were records!

definitions.text: Relating to time before CDs? No, in fact before there were records!

parts.note: surface reading: an era before compact discs, when music came on vinyl records
setter's reading: records as written history, so the time before any history was written down

explanation.walkthrough: The clue starts with music formats, then switches 'records' from discs to historical documents.
explanation.definitionFit: Prehistoric describes the period before written history, when no records of events were kept.

clue.text: From another writer this would be appropriate

definitions.text: From another writer this would be appropriate

parts.note: surface reading: appropriate as an adjective, meaning suitable
setter's reading: appropriate as a verb, to take someone else's words as one's own

explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' looks like the adjective meaning fitting, but it is the verb meaning to seize.
explanation.definitionFit: To plagiarise is to steal another author's work and pass it off as one's own.

clue.text: Pointers to scheming unnecessarily

parts.note: needles on dials and compasses point
sly means cunning or scheming

explanation.surface: Signs that someone is plotting without any need.
explanation.definitionFit: Needlessly means without any good reason or requirement, so done when it need not be.

clue.text: Putting less on when Bare Rock's running

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective, 'wearing less'

indicators.note: the answer runs along the clue's letters, continuing from one word into the next

parts.note: the letters run from the start of Bare into the start of Rock's

explanation.surface: Wearing fewer clothes when the band Bare Rock is performing.
explanation.definitionFit: Barer is the comparative of bare, so someone barer is less clothed, as if wearing less.

clue.text: Recover Ecstasy round the City

indicators.note: round means encircling, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: rapture is ecstatic joy
EC is the postcode of the City of London, the financial district

explanation.surface: Someone takes back the ecstasy drug being passed around London's financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ecstasy' suggests E for the drug, but here it is the emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: To recapture is to take back or regain something lost, as one might recover it.

clue.text: Mug to estimate apparent worth

parts.note: mug is slang for the face
to value something is to estimate its worth

explanation.surface: Someone appraises a mug to see what it is apparently worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' looks like a cup to be valued, but it is slang for a face.
explanation.definitionFit: Face value is the worth printed on a coin or note, hence how something seems on the surface.

clue.text: Simplicity once in unusual new church

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters appear in an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A plain style once found in an unusual modern church building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link placing once inside something, but its letters join the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Innocence can mean artlessness or naivety, a guileless simplicity of character.

clue.text: Formal, chilly, not initially friendly

indicators.note: not means without, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: frigid means very cold

indicators.note: initially points to the beginning, so just the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of friendly

explanation.surface: Someone stiff and cold who is unfriendly at first meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'not initially friendly' as a description of a person; it actually removes friendly's first letter from the cold word.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigid can mean strict and inflexible, as in stiffly formal manners or rules.

clue.text: Walk around to keep youngsters on the move?

parts.note: surface reading: simply to stroll about

parts.words: to keep youngsters on the move
parts.note: setter's reading: what a perambulator, or pram, does with babies

explanation.walkthrough: A pram is short for perambulator, so the verb sounds like what a pram is for. Pram is the British word for a baby carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: To perambulate is a formal word for to stroll or walk about a place.

clue.text: Remove the weapons during the lunar month

indicators.note: during means within a span, so the answer lies within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of lunar and the start of month

explanation.surface: A truce means disarming for the duration of one lunar month.
explanation.definitionFit: To unarm is an older word for disarm, to take away someone's weapons.

clue.text: Go nuts after getting a rise

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read from the bottom up

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy, as is nuts

explanation.surface: Someone flies into a rage after being teased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go nuts' reads as one phrase, but 'Go' is the definition and 'nuts' the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a stab at something is to have a go, an attempt or try.

clue.text: Worry? Strings could be attached!

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a raised ridge across a guitar neck, which strings are pressed against

explanation.walkthrough: 'Strings attached' plays on the idiom about hidden conditions, a fair thing to worry over.
explanation.definitionFit: To fret is to be anxious, and a fret is a bar on a stringed instrument's fingerboard.

clue.text: Address, say, the force in rotation

indicators.note: say asks us to speak a word and listen to how it comes out

parts.note: to address an audience is to give a talk; in a non-rhotic British accent the two words sound the same

explanation.surface: A lecture on the physics of rotating forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Torque is the turning force, the moment of force that produces rotation about an axis.

clue.text: East wind fades and becomes more stable

indicators.note: to wind is to twist and coil, so the letters are twisted out of order

parts.note: taken as written
a sound or light that fades dies away

explanation.surface: An easterly breeze dies down and the weather settles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' reads as the noun, a breeze from the east, but it is the verb meaning twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadies is a verb meaning makes or grows firm and settled, so becoming more stable.

clue.text: Beat up the flour and eggs

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a mixture of flour, eggs and milk for cooking

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a recipe step, beating up flour and eggs; but the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Batter is both a verb for pounding something hard and a noun for the runny mix used for pancakes.

clue.text: Sparking rhymes I'm excited about

indicators.note: something excited is stirred up and agitated, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters of both words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A poet is thrilled by the sparkle of their own rhymes.
explanation.definitionFit: Shimmery means glinting with a soft flickering light, close to sparkling.
